title: Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded at admission, considered automatically through the NUS undergraduate admission application with no separate scholarship application
funding_type: Full coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees plus living, accommodation and one-time allowances, university-funded, subject to a six-year service bond
administering_authority: National University of Singapore (NUS), Office of Admissions
implementing_agency: NUS Office of Admissions (same body that runs the scheme)
programme_action: NUS Office of Admissions freshmen scholarship portfolio - "Scholarships for Freshmen (International Students)" and "Scholarships for Freshmen (Singapore Permanent Residents)", scholarship type "University-Level"
description: The Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship is a freshmen scholarship offered by the National University of Singapore to support outstanding Asian students (excluding Singapore citizens). Candidates are considered and shortlisted for the scholarship through their application for undergraduate admission to NUS; there is no separate scholarship application or scholarship deadline. The award provides 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, a S$6,000 annual living allowance, a S$1,750 one-time computer allowance upon enrolment, a S$200 one-time settling-in allowance upon enrolment, an annual accommodation allowance equivalent to the lowest double room rate for on-campus accommodation, and a travel allowance for the incoming and return passage. Recipients must serve a six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation, must take up the MOE Tuition Grant, and the scholarship is renewed every semester provided the scholar maintains a GPA of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) and has good conduct.

award_types: Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship (single award type; NUS publishes no tiers or variants of this award)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: One award type, restricted by field of study rather than by tier. NUS states that the scholarship is awarded to freshmen pursuing the listed full-time undergraduate programmes, and that it also covers students in local Double Degree Programmes provided the scholarship recipient's home programme falls within one of the listed programmes.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: The scholarship will be renewed every semester, provided the scholar maintains a Grade Point Average (GPA) of at least 3.50 (or equivalent), and has good conduct. Renewal is also subject to the award-holder conditions, including that at least 75% of the credits/units required for graduation are earned in Singapore and that overseas programmes are completed before September of the year prior to graduation.
programme_structure.intake: Assessed through the live NUS undergraduate admissions cycle. The official Important Dates and Application page records the application period for this scholarship as "Based on admissions application timeline", with the note "All eligible students will be considered for the scholarship through their application for undergraduate admission to NUS." Selection interview(s) are conducted from January to July and interviewed candidates are informed of the scholarship outcomes by mid-July.

status_label: Open - automatic consideration through the NUS admissions cycle
status_note: The award has no scholarship window of its own and no published closing date: NUS states that all eligible students will be considered for the scholarship through their application for undergraduate admission to NUS, so the award is assessed continuously against the NUS undergraduate admissions timeline for the applicant's qualification. As at the verification date the award page carried no closed notice, no waitlist notice and no paused-intake notice, so the cycle is treated as open for the coming intake. The eligibility gate is a citizenship test (citizens of an Asian country or region, excluding Singapore) rather than a nationality quota, and NUS reserves the right not to award any scholarship if there are no candidates of sufficient merit.
verification_type: Official university website (nus.edu.sg, Office of Admissions) plus the official Singapore Ministry of Education Tuition Grant Scheme pages (moe.gov.sg).
verification_notes: Read the official NUS Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship page (both the International Students and the Singapore Permanent Residents versions, which carry identical terms), the NUS Scholarships Important Dates and Application page, the NUS Office of Admissions scholarships catalogue page, the NUS admissions Important Dates page, and the NUS Office of the University Registrar MOE Tuition Grant and fees page, plus the MOE Tuition Grant Scheme overview and Employment and pass matters pages. Every amount, eligibility criterion, bond term, renewal threshold and credit-distribution rule in this record was taken verbatim from those pages. Nine official-domain sources were read; no third-party aggregator, listing site, news article or stock source was used for any fact.
source_last_updated: The NUS Office of Admissions pages carry no published last-updated date. The MOE Tuition Grant Scheme pages used for the bond terms are stamped "Last Updated: 23 Jun 2026". The NUS admissions Important Dates page currently publishes the Academic Year 2027/2028 windows and marks every application period as [Closed].

application_deadline.typical_application_window: No scholarship window exists. The official Important Dates and Application page records the application period for the Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship as "Based on admissions application timeline", that is, the NUS undergraduate admissions application period for the applicant's own qualification. For reference, the NUS admissions Important Dates page published Academic Year 2027/2028 windows of 16 December 2026 to 4 January 2027 (NUS High School Diploma), 16 December 2026 to 3 February 2027 (Polytechnic Diploma from Singapore), 16 December 2026 to 17 February 2027 (IB Diploma and International Qualifications except IB Diploma) and 18 February 2027 (late afternoon) to 19 March 2027 (Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level), each shown as closed at the time of verification. For this scholarship the only dates NUS publishes are that selection interview(s) are conducted from January to July and that interviewed candidates are informed of the scholarship outcomes by mid-July.
application_deadline.application_period: No separate scholarship application period. Consideration is automatic through the NUS undergraduate admission application, so the effective window is the admissions application period for the applicant's qualification.
application_deadline.official_rule: NUS: "All eligible students will be considered for this scholarship through their application for undergraduate admission to NUS." The Official Important Dates and Application page lists the application period for the Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship as "Based on admissions application timeline" and the qualification requirement as "High school qualifications eligible for admission to NUS". The 1 February to 19 March 2027 window published on the same page belongs to NUS Scholarships for Freshmen (Singapore Citizens) and is expressly not this award's window.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: Do not treat the 1 February to 19 March 2027 window on the Important Dates page as this scholarship's deadline; NUS applies that window to the Singapore Citizen NUS Scholarships. Because there is no scholarship deadline of its own, an applicant who misses the NUS admissions application period for their qualification cannot recover by applying separately for the scholarship. deadline_date is null because NUS publishes no calendar date for this award.

programme_duration.official_range: Tenable for the normal candidature period of the undergraduate programme at NUS. NUS publishes no fixed number of years for this award; the duration follows the candidature period of the specific degree programme entered, and local Double Degree Programme students are covered provided their home programme is one of the listed programmes.
programme_duration.renewal_note: Renewed every semester on condition that the scholar maintains a GPA of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) and has good conduct, and continues to satisfy the award-holder conditions including the 75% in-Singapore credit rule.

funding.scholarship_type: University-level merit scholarship awarded at admission, considered automatically with the NUS undergraduate admission application
funding.monthly_amount_note: No monthly stipend is paid. The recurring cash benefit is a S$6,000 annual living allowance plus an annual accommodation allowance set by reference to the lowest on-campus double room rate; NUS publishes no monthly rate.
funding.travel_amount_note: NUS states the travel allowance "defray[s] transport cost for incoming passage from home country to Singapore at the start of Programme, and return passage between Singapore and home country after the completion of Programme (subject to proof of employment)". No per-passage amount, cap or claim procedure is published.
funding.institutional_costs: NUS publishes no aggregate institutional cost or budget for this scholarship. The only published monetary values are the S$6,000 annual living allowance, the S$1,750 one-time computer allowance and the S$200 one-time settling-in allowance; the tuition element is a coverage statement against subsidised fees rather than a sum, and the accommodation allowance is expressed as a room rate rather than a sum.
funding.fully_funded_note: Not unconditionally fully funded. Tuition coverage is stated only against subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, which recipients are required to take up, so the gap to the full non-subsidised international rate is not covered. The award also carries a six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation, and the required MOE Tuition Grant carries its own three-year bond for Permanent Residents and international students. NUS states it does not guarantee and/or provide scholarship recipients with employment upon graduation.

tuition.conditions: 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees (after MOE Tuition Grant - scholarship recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant). No monetary figure is published and coverage is stated only against the subsidised rate.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published in official source - the award pays an annual living allowance, not a monthly stipend.

travel_allowance.conditions: Travel allowance to defray transport cost for incoming passage from home country to Singapore at the start of the programme, and return passage between Singapore and home country after completion of the programme (subject to proof of employment). No amount is published.

installation_allowance.conditions: S$200 one-time settling-in allowance upon enrolment.

equipment_allowance.conditions: S$1,750 one-time computer allowance upon enrolment.

accommodation_support.conditions: Annual accommodation allowance equivalent to the lowest double room rate for on-campus accommodation. NUS publishes no monetary figure; it states the allowance only by reference to the room rate.

bond.conditions: Scholarship recipients are required to serve a six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation. Separately, recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant, and Permanent Residents and international students who receive a Tuition Grant are required to work for a Singapore entity for three years upon graduation (employed full-time in a Singapore entity for 3 years to fulfil the bond obligations).

total_estimated_value.note: No total value is computed or presented as an award. The tuition element is a coverage statement against subsidised fees, the accommodation allowance is expressed as a room rate rather than a sum, and the travel allowance is unquantified by NUS, so any headline total would be invented.

coverage: 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees (after MOE Tuition Grant - scholarship recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant)
S$1,750 one-time computer allowance upon enrolment
S$200 one-time settling-in allowance upon enrolment
Annual accommodation allowance equivalent to the lowest double room rate for on-campus accommodation

Travel allowance to defray transport cost for incoming passage from home country to Singapore at the start of the programme, and return passage between Singapore and home country after completion of the programme (subject to proof of employment)
coverage_limitations: Tuition coverage is stated only against subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant; the difference between the subsidised and the full non-subsidised international tuition rate is not covered, and NUS states that students who do not complete the MOE Tuition Grant application and signing by the stipulated deadlines will be charged the non-subsidised tuition fees.

Recipients are required to take up the MOE Tuition Grant, which itself carries a three-year bond to work for a Singapore entity after graduation for Permanent Residents and international students, in addition to the scholarship's own six-year bond.
The accommodation allowance is capped at the lowest double room rate for on-campus accommodation; NUS publishes no monetary figure for it.
The travel allowance covers only the incoming passage and the return passage, and the return passage is subject to proof of employment; personal travel is not covered.
NUS does not guarantee and/or provide scholarship recipients with employment upon graduation, so the six-year bond is a real post-graduation constraint rather than a formality.
Besides the MOE Tuition Grant, recipients may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance.
Exact benefit structure may differ in future cycles; all amounts and terms quoted here are those published on the official page at the verification date.
eligible_applicants: Citizens of an Asian country or region, excluding Singapore
Applicants with outstanding high school results
Applicants with an excellent co-curricular activities record
Applicants with strong leadership qualities and potential

Applicants applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme in Computing, Engineering (excluding Infrastructure and Project Management) or Science (excluding Environmental Studies and Pharmacy) at NUS
Freshmen entering one of the specific full-time undergraduate programmes listed in the scholarship Terms and Conditions
Students in local Double Degree Programmes whose home programme falls within one of the listed programmes
Holders of a high school qualification eligible for admission to NUS
final_year_condition: Not applicable in the bachelor's-degree sense. This is a freshmen admission scholarship, so the qualifying credential is a high-school qualification: NUS states the qualification requirement as "High school qualifications eligible for admission to NUS". Final-year high-school students applying for first-year admission to NUS are the intended applicants. Transfer applicants from local or overseas universities are not eligible.
equivalent_degree_note: Yes, by reference. The scholarship publishes no qualification list of its own; it adopts the NUS admissions rule "High school qualifications eligible for admission to NUS", which NUS administers across Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level, Polytechnic Diploma from Singapore, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma and International Qualifications (except IB Diploma). Whether a particular foreign school-leaving qualification counts is decided by the NUS undergraduate admissions process, not by the scholarship terms.
previous_award_restriction: Scholarship recipients are required to take up the MOE Tuition Grant. Besides this, they may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance. No restriction on having previously applied for, or held, this same scholarship is published.

eligibility.citizenship: Citizens of an Asian country or region, excluding Singapore. NUS also labels the award's nationality band as "Singapore Permanent Residents / International Students" and publishes the award under both the Singapore Permanent Residents and the International Students sections, while the eligibility criterion is written as a citizenship test. Applicants who are Singapore citizens, or who are citizens of a country or region outside Asia, are not eligible.
eligibility.residence_requirement: None published. NUS states no residence or domicile requirement for this scholarship; the gate is the citizenship test above.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Yes. The qualification requirement is "High school qualifications eligible for admission to NUS", and an eligibility criterion is to possess outstanding high school results.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Possess outstanding high school results. NUS publishes no percentage, grade-point average or rank cut-off for high-school performance.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No high-school GPA threshold is published for admission to the award. The published GPA threshold applies after enrolment: the scholarship is renewed every semester provided the scholar maintains a Grade Point Average (GPA) of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) and has good conduct.
eligibility.language_requirement: None published on the scholarship page. English proficiency is handled through the separate NUS undergraduate admissions process; no language test, score or certificate is named for this scholarship.
eligibility.work_experience: Not required and not published as a criterion.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Yes - "Have strong leadership qualities and potential".
eligibility.financial_need: No. The award is not means-tested; NUS publishes no income, asset or family-circumstance test for it.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Besides the MOE Tuition Grant, scholarship recipients may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Freshmen only. Applicants must be applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS, and transfer applicants from local or overseas universities are not eligible.
eligibility.field_restrictions: The award is restricted to the full-time undergraduate programmes named in the Terms and Conditions. School of Computing: Artificial Intelligence, Business Analytics, Business Artificial Intelligence Systems, Computer Science, Information Security. College of Design and Engineering: engineering majors only - Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Engineering Science, Environmental and Sustainability Engineering, Industrial & Systems Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Robotics & Machine Intelligence. School of Computing and College of Design and Engineering: Computer Engineering. College of Humanities and Sciences: science majors only, excluding Environmental Studies and Pharmacy - Chemistry, Data Science and Analytics, Data Science and Economics, Food Science and Technology, Geospatial Intelligence, Life Sciences, Mathematics, Pharmaceutical Science, Physics, Quantitative Finance, and Statistics. The field restriction is stated twice: applicants must be applying for admission to a programme in Computing, Engineering (excluding Infrastructure and Project Management) or Science (excluding Environmental Studies and Pharmacy) at NUS, and must be entering one of the programmes listed above. Students in local Double Degree Programmes are covered only if the home programme falls within the listed programmes.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No high-school percentage or equivalent numerical threshold is published. NUS states the criterion qualitatively as "Possess outstanding high school results", so no universal percentage field can be filled.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: The applicant must be entering one of the specific full-time undergraduate programmes listed in the Terms and Conditions (School of Computing; College of Design and Engineering engineering majors only; College of Humanities and Sciences science majors only, excluding Environmental Studies and Pharmacy; and Computer Engineering under School of Computing and College of Design and Engineering). Engineering excludes Infrastructure and Project Management and Science excludes Environmental Studies and Pharmacy.
selection_factors_may_include: Strength of the application for undergraduate admission to NUS overall
Entry into one of the eligible Computing, Engineering or Science programmes
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: NUS states that "Invited applicants will be assessed for scholarship suitability based on the strength of their application" and publishes no numerical weighting among high school results, co-curricular record, leadership and interview performance. NUS reserves the right not to award any scholarship if there are no candidates of sufficient merit, and the decision of the selection committee is final with enquiries or disputes not entertained.

english_requirement.moi_rule: No medium-of-instruction rule is published for this scholarship. English requirements are a condition of admission to NUS, administered through the NUS undergraduate admissions process, and are not stated on the scholarship page.
english_requirement.test_score_note: The NUS Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship page publishes no English language test, score or certificate requirement, so every score field here is null.

language_of_instruction.language_note: The language of instruction is set by each NUS degree programme, not by this award, and the scholarship page publishes no information about it. The scholarship page itself is published in English only. Applicants should confirm the language of instruction on the individual NUS programme page.

application_method.application_route: No separate scholarship application. Consideration is automatic through the NUS undergraduate admission application submitted via the NUS Applicant Portal; only applicants shortlisted for the selection interview(s) are informed via e-mail.
application_steps: Confirm you are a citizen of an Asian country or region other than Singapore, since the award is closed to Singapore citizens and to citizens of countries outside Asia.

Choose a full-time first-degree programme that appears on the official eligible-programme list, checking that it is not Infrastructure and Project Management (Engineering) or Environmental Studies or Pharmacy (Science).
Hold, or be completing, a high school qualification eligible for admission to NUS and assemble results that show outstanding high school performance.
Build and document an excellent co-curricular activities record and leadership roles, because both are explicit eligibility criteria and the application is assessed on its overall strength.

Submit a single application for undergraduate admission to NUS through the NUS Applicant Portal within the admissions application period for your qualification; there is no scholarship form, scholarship portal submission or scholarship deadline.
Wait for NUS to make contact: only applicants shortlisted for the selection interview(s) are informed via e-mail.
Attend the selection interview(s), which are conducted from January to July, if shortlisted.

On award, take up the MOE Tuition Grant and complete the MOE Tuition Grant application and signing, and accept the scholarship terms including the six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation.
Maintain a GPA of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) and good conduct each semester, and keep at least 75% of the credits/units required for graduation earned in Singapore.
application_method.application_fee: No scholarship application fee is published, because there is no separate scholarship application. Any NUS undergraduate admission application fee is set by the NUS admissions process and is not published on the scholarship page.

official_application_documents.document_format: Not published on the scholarship page. The only submission is the NUS undergraduate admission application; NUS publishes no scholarship-specific form, upload or format for this award.
official_application_documents.transcript_requirement: Not published as a scholarship requirement. NUS states only that applicants hold "High school qualifications eligible for admission to NUS"; the transcript and result documents required are those of the NUS undergraduate admission application.
official_application_documents.certified_translation_requirement: Not published on the scholarship page. Translation requirements, where they apply, are set by the NUS undergraduate admissions process.

academic_documents.notes: Stated on the Important Dates and Application page as the qualification requirement for the Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship. The document set itself is whatever the NUS undergraduate admission application requires; the scholarship page publishes no separate document list.

additional_documents.notes: Because there is no separate scholarship application, NUS publishes no scholarship form, essay, referee report, portfolio or financial document for this award. Shortlisted candidates are contacted by e-mail for the selection interview.

selection_process.weighting_note: NUS publishes no numerical weighting or scoring formula among high school results, co-curricular record, leadership and interview performance, so selection_weighting and official_universal_weighting are null.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: The scholarship funds a full-time NUS undergraduate degree programme in Computing, Engineering or Science; it does not itself award a separate qualification.
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: Set by each NUS degree programme. NUS states the scholarship is tenable for the normal candidature period of the undergraduate programme at NUS but publishes no fixed number of years.
possible_awards: Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship (single award type)
degree_outcome.degree_note: This is an admission scholarship for freshmen. Applicants must be applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS; transfer applicants from local or overseas universities are not eligible.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Addressed indirectly through the credit-distribution rule: overseas programmes must be completed before September of the year prior to graduation, and at least 75% of the credits/units required for graduation must be earned in Singapore with no more than 25% obtained through overseas programmes. NUS's own example: if 160 units are required to graduate, a maximum of 40 units may be earned through overseas programmes.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Subsidised undergraduate tuition fees are fully covered, after the MOE Tuition Grant, and recipients are required to take up the MOE Tuition Grant. Students who do not complete the MOE Tuition Grant application and signing by the stipulated deadlines are charged the non-subsidised tuition fees by NUS.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No scholarship application fee, because there is no separate scholarship application for this award.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: On award, recipients take up the MOE Tuition Grant, applying and signing through the MOE Tuition Grant and Scholarships portal, and accept the scholarship terms. Those terms require a six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation, bar concurrent holding of any other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance besides the MOE Tuition Grant, require semesterly renewal at a GPA of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) with good conduct, and require at least 75% of graduation credits to be earned in Singapore with overseas programmes completed before September of the year prior to graduation. NUS reserves the right to impose repayment of all scholarship monies disbursed if the recipient withdraws from the University and/or terminates the scholarship prematurely.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: NUS publishes no scholarship-specific student services. The accommodation element is an annual allowance equivalent to the lowest double room rate for on-campus accommodation, and the computer element is a one-time S$1,750 computer allowance upon enrolment.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: Six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation. Separately, recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant, and Singapore Permanent Residents and international students who receive a Tuition Grant are required to work for a Singapore entity for three years upon graduation, employed full-time in a Singapore entity for 3 years to fulfil the bond obligations.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: NUS states that it does not guarantee and/or provide scholarship recipients with employment upon graduation, and that if the scholarship recipient decides to withdraw from the University and/or terminate the scholarship prematurely, the University reserves the right to impose repayment of all scholarship monies disbursed to the scholar. For the MOE Tuition Grant bond, MOE publishes liquidated-damages consequences where there are changes to course status or where a recipient buys out the bond, and provides a bond-deferment process.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a citizen of an Asian country or region other than Singapore, because the award is closed to Singapore citizens and to citizens of countries outside Asia
Check your intended programme against the official eligible-programme list before applying, because the award does not cover every Computing, Engineering or Science programme
Rule out Infrastructure and Project Management under Engineering and Environmental Studies and Pharmacy under Science, which are expressly excluded
Confirm you are not applying as a transfer applicant from a local or overseas university
If entering a Double Degree Programme, confirm which programme is your home programme, since coverage depends on it
Hold, or be completing, a high school qualification eligible for admission to NUS and assemble results showing outstanding performance
Assemble documented evidence of co-curricular activities and leadership, since NUS assesses suitability on the strength of the application
Submit the single NUS undergraduate admission application within the admissions application period for your qualification - there is no separate scholarship form or deadline
Be available between January and July for the selection interview if NUS contacts you by e-mail
Plan for the six-year post-graduation bond with a Singapore-registered company before accepting, and for the three-year MOE Tuition Grant bond that comes with the required Tuition Grant
Review any planned overseas exchange or study-abroad load against the 75% in-Singapore credit rule before committing

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: No scholarship-specific essay or motivation letter is required, because there is no separate scholarship application. The strategic equivalent is the NUS undergraduate admission application itself, which NUS assesses for scholarship suitability: make outstanding high-school results, the co-curricular record and leadership visible there, since only applicants shortlisted on the strength of that application are contacted for the selection interview.
profile_fit_labels: Outstanding Asian high-school leaver (excluding Singapore citizens) applying to a first-year NUS degree
Applicant targeting NUS Computing, Engineering or Science
Applicant with a strong co-curricular record and demonstrated leadership
Applicant willing to accept a six-year post-graduation bond with a Singapore-registered company
Applicant willing to take up the MOE Tuition Grant and its bond
Applicant who can keep at least 75% of graduation credits in Singapore
common_mistakes: Assuming this is a separate scholarship you apply for after admission - NUS considers all eligible students through the undergraduate admission application
Applying to a programme outside the official list, for example Infrastructure and Project Management under Engineering, or Environmental Studies or Pharmacy under Science
Holding a nationality outside Asia, or being a Singapore citizen, neither of which is eligible
Applying as a transfer applicant from a local or overseas university, which is expressly ineligible
Missing the NUS admissions application period for your qualification, because there is no separate scholarship window to fall back on
Assuming the 1 February to 19 March 2027 window applies to this award - that window belongs to NUS Scholarships for Freshmen (Singapore Citizens)
Believing the award covers the full non-subsidised international tuition rate - coverage is stated only against subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant
Ignoring the six-year bond, on the assumption that NUS arranges employment - NUS states it does not guarantee and/or provide employment upon graduation
Falling below a GPA of 3.50, since the scholarship is reviewed and renewed every semester
Holding another scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance concurrently besides the MOE Tuition Grant
Planning an overseas programme or exchange load above 25% of graduation credits, or leaving an overseas programme unfinished past September of the year before graduation
Withdrawing from NUS or terminating the scholarship early, which can trigger repayment of all scholarship monies disbursed
Assuming this is the same award as the NUS International Undergraduate Scholarship, which is open to citizens of all countries except Singapore and is already a separate record in this database

risk_flags.risk: Six-year service bond and no employment guarantee
risk_flags.impact: Recipients must serve a six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation, while NUS states it does not guarantee and/or provide employment upon graduation, so a graduate who cannot secure a qualifying Singapore position is exposed.
risk_flags.mitigation: Record the bond in funding_breakdown.bond and student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement, and set fully_funded to false so the award is never presented as an unconditional full ride.

risk_flags.impact: Only citizens of an Asian country or region, excluding Singapore, are eligible; applicants from outside Asia and Singapore citizens themselves cannot hold this award.
risk_flags.mitigation: Set citizenship_restriction to true and worldwide_eligibility to false, and state the gate in eligible_applicants, not_best_fit and eligibility.citizenship so it is not overstated as a worldwide award.

risk_flags.risk: No scholarship deadline of its own
risk_flags.impact: Because consideration is automatic through the admissions application, an applicant who misses the NUS admissions application period for their qualification has no separate scholarship window to fall back on, and deadlines vary by qualification.
risk_flags.mitigation: Set deadline_date to null with deadline_precision "programme_specific", quote NUS's "Based on admissions application timeline" wording in official_rule, and warn against reusing the Singapore Citizen window.

risk_flags.impact: The award covers only the listed Computing, Engineering and Science programmes, excluding Infrastructure and Project Management under Engineering and Environmental Studies and Pharmacy under Science, so an otherwise strong applicant in an excluded programme receives nothing.
risk_flags.mitigation: Reproduce the full official programme list in eligibility.field_restrictions and flag the two named exclusions in coverage_limitations, risk flags and not_best_fit.

risk_flags.risk: Tuition coverage is stated only against subsidised fees
risk_flags.impact: Coverage is 100% of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, which recipients must take up; the gap to the full non-subsidised international rate is not covered, and failing the Tuition Grant signing deadlines triggers non-subsidised fees.
risk_flags.mitigation: State the subsidised basis explicitly in funding.tuition and coverage_limitations, and record the MOE Tuition Grant requirement in the bond and student-agreement fields.

risk_flags.risk: Semesterly renewal at a GPA of 3.50
risk_flags.impact: The scholarship is renewed every semester only if the scholar maintains a GPA of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) and has good conduct, so a single weak semester puts the award at risk.
risk_flags.mitigation: Record the renewal threshold in programme_structure.renewal_criteria, programme_duration.renewal_note and eligibility.gpa_requirement, and list it among common mistakes.

risk_flags.risk: Several benefit amounts are published only as rates or passages, not sums
risk_flags.impact: The accommodation allowance is expressed as the lowest on-campus double room rate and the travel allowance covers named passages without any amount, so any quoted "total award value" would be invented.
risk_flags.mitigation: Keep amount fields null for those elements, prohibit a computed total in funding_breakdown.total_estimated_value, and list the gaps in verification.unverified_or_removed_claims.

risk_flags.impact: Besides the MOE Tuition Grant, recipients may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance, which forecloses stacking this award with other funding.
risk_flags.mitigation: Record the restriction in previous_award_restriction, eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction and coverage_limitations.

Applicant submits the single NUS undergraduate admission application through the Applicant Portal
All eligible students applying for undergraduate admission are considered for this scholarship
NUS assesses invited applicants for scholarship suitability based on the strength of their application
Shortlisted applicants are informed via e-mail
Selection interview(s) conducted from January to July
Outcomes communicated to interviewed candidates by mid-July
On award, MOE Tuition Grant offer accepted and signed through the MOE Tuition Grant and Scholarships portal
Scholarship acceptance terms accepted, including the six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company

Graduation, followed by the six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company and the three-year MOE Tuition Grant bond
best_fit: An outstanding high-school leaver who is a citizen of an Asian country or region other than Singapore, holds outstanding high school results with an excellent co-curricular record and demonstrated leadership, and is applying for first-year admission to a full-time NUS degree programme on the eligible list in Computing, Engineering or Science. The award suits an applicant who is willing to take up the MOE Tuition Grant, to accept a six-year post-graduation bond with a Singapore-registered company, to forgo any other concurrent scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance, and to keep at least 75% of the credits required for graduation earned in Singapore.

image.logo_verification_method: Probed the asset directly on the official nus.edu.sg domain. https://nus.edu.sg/images/default-source/base/logo.png returned HTTP 200 with Content-Type image/png and 26,329 bytes, with the PNG signature (89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A) confirmed on the first bytes, 300 x 137 pixels, Format32bppArgb. The bytes were downloaded and visually inspected: it is the NUS institutional mark, a navy shield with an open book and a ring above an orange lion, beside the dark-blue "NUS" wordmark and the words "National University of Singapore", on a transparent field. It is not a white-on-transparent wordmark and is safe on a light card. The identical asset was also confirmed at http-200 with Content-Type image/png and 26,329 bytes on www.nus.edu.sg. A second official mark was verified the same way: https://nus.edu.sg/oam/assets/OAM_Revamp/images/logo-nus.png, the masthead mark rendered on the scholarship page itself, HTTP 200, Content-Type image/png, 11,114 bytes, 146 x 67, same crest and wordmark. The awarding body is NUS itself, so the NUS institutional mark is the correct logo; no ministry, aggregator, CDN or third-party mark was used.

database_notes: DUPLICATION CHECK: this record is deliberately distinct from the NUS International Undergraduate Scholarship already in the do-not-duplicate list, which is open to citizens of all countries except Singapore and carries different benefits. The Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship is field-restricted to Computing, Engineering and Science, is limited to citizens of an Asian country or region excluding Singapore, and carries a six-year bond.
NUS also administers an ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship from the same Office of Admissions; it is a different award with a different citizenship gate (ASEAN countries only) and is not recorded here.

The award is published by NUS under both "Scholarships for Freshmen (Singapore Permanent Residents)" and "Scholarships for Freshmen (International Students)". Both versions were read and carry identical scholarship benefits, terms and conditions, programme list and shortlisting process. The eligibility criteria reproduced here are NUS's own wording, which frames the award as support for outstanding Asian students excluding Singapore citizens while labelling the nationality band as Singapore Permanent Residents / International Students. NUS does not publish whether the two are assessed on identical terms.
SHORT TITLE: NUS publishes no acronym or short form for this award. "S&TUS" is a clear short form created for this database and is not an official NUS abbreviation.
LEGACY TITLES: none. NUS publishes no alternative or former name for this award, so legacy_titles is an empty array rather than a guessed one.

DEGREE LEVEL: confirmed at bachelor's level directly from the awarding body. The page labels the award "Student Type: Freshmen", describes it as "a freshmen scholarship offered to support outstanding Asian students (excluding Singapore citizens)", requires applicants to be "Applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme ... at NUS", states the scholarship "is tenable for the normal candidature period of the undergraduate programme at NUS", and the Important Dates and Application page states the qualification requirement as "High school qualifications eligible for admission to NUS". No master's, doctoral or research component appears in the official text.

ADMISSION VERSUS FUNDING: this is an admission-linked award that is considered automatically through the undergraduate admission application. There is no separate scholarship application, no scholarship form, no scholarship portal submission, no scholarship deadline and no scholarship fee. This is recorded explicitly in application_method (direct_student_application and central_application both false, automatic_consideration true) and in programme_structure.application_required false.

BOND: the scholarship carries a six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation. Recipients must also take up the MOE Tuition Grant, which for Singapore Permanent Residents and international students carries a separate three-year bond requiring full-time employment in a Singapore entity after graduation. NUS states it does not guarantee and/or provide employment upon graduation. For these reasons fully_funded is false and the award is never presented as an unconditional full ride.

TUITION BASIS: coverage is stated only against subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant. The difference between the subsidised and the full non-subsidised international rate is not covered, and the NUS fees page states that eligible students who do not complete the MOE Tuition Grant application and signing by the stipulated deadlines will be charged the non-subsidised tuition fees. No current fee figures are quoted here because they are published annually and were not read as a fee table in this session.

DEADLINE: deadline_date is null with deadline_precision "programme_specific" because NUS publishes no calendar date for this scholarship, only "Based on admissions application timeline". The Academic Year 2027/2028 admissions windows quoted in typical_application_window are quoted for context from the NUS admissions Important Dates page and were all marked [Closed] at the verification date; they are not this scholarship's deadlines. The 1 February to 19 March 2027 window on the scholarship Important Dates page applies to NUS Scholarships for Freshmen (Singapore Citizens) only and is expressly not attributed here.

UNPUBLISHED AMOUNTS: no sum is published for the accommodation allowance (stated only as the lowest on-campus double room rate) or for the travel allowance (stated only as the incoming and return passage, return subject to proof of employment). No monthly stipend, aggregate budget, number of awards, age limit, gender restriction, nationality quota, English test score, selection weighting or scholarship document list is published. These are recorded as null or empty rather than filled with plausible values.

LOGO: the NUS institutional mark was verified live on the official nus.edu.sg domain (two assets, both HTTP 200 with Content-Type image/png and confirmed PNG signatures, downloaded and visually inspected). The awarding body is NUS itself, so the university mark is the correct logo. No logo was taken from any aggregator, CDN, third-party site or other awarding body.

RESEARCH DATE: SCHEMA_CONTRACT.md states the batch research date as 2026-10-03 and requires that exact date for last_verified_date, _verification_timestamp, logo_verified_at and image_verified_at, so those fields use 2026-10-03 for consistency with the rest of the dataset. The NUS and MOE pages were read in a session whose local clock showed 2026-10-10, and the page contents matched the cycle already recorded for this award.

FETCH RECORD: nine official-domain pages were read for this record (seven NUS pages including both published versions of the award page, plus two MOE Tuition Grant Scheme pages), and three logo assets were probed on the official nus.edu.sg domain. No third-party aggregator, scholarship-listing site, news article, blog or stock source was used for any fact in this record.
